claims.text: Introducing a hierarchical microstructure combining coarse and fine grains can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The intervention produces a hierarchical grain-size distribution and altered grain-boundary interactions.
Coarse grains in the hierarchical microstructure provide strength.
Fine grains in the hierarchical microstructure provide ductility.
Grain-boundary interactions in the hierarchical microstructure enhance overall mechanical properties.
The hierarchical microstructure will increase strength by 10–20% relative to a non-hierarchical microstructure.
The hierarchical microstructure will increase ductility by 15–30% relative to a non-hierarchical microstructure.
The intervention is effective within a grain-size range that permits an optimal strength–ductility balance.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
